# Fear System
[bold]The Fear System is a global mechanic that influences player interaction with SCPs, as well as player interaction with the consequences of SCP containment breaches.[/bold]
[bold]Fear is a game mechanic designed to enhance immersion. It serves as a form of feedback between the character's actions and the player, allowing the character's emotions to be conveyed to the player.[/bold]
## How does it work?
All characters have their own fears. The standard phobias for every Foundation employee are: - [bold]Exoremophobia[/bold] — The fear of external reality streams and alien courses of events. It manifests as a fear of SCPs. - [bold]Necrophobia[/bold] — The fear of corpses, dead bodies, and anything else associated with the dead.
These fears influence what the character will be afraid of. You can view the current fears in the character window, in the section where the antagonists' goals are listed.
Furthermore, all the characters have several levels of fear.
- None: You are calm. - Anxiety: Something is wrong. - Fear: You are frightened of something. - Uncontrollable Terror: SOMETHING is too REAL for you to come to terms with. It is a nightmare. This amount of fear is only accessible through mind-altering anomalous effects, such as those offered by SCP-035 or SCP-012.
[bold]Characters may become frightened upon sighting a source of fear or approaching it.[/bold] Of course, there are exceptions. Certain facility personnel have grown accustomed to observing "frightening" objects, and as a result, such encounters do not faze them.
For instance, researchers are prepared for the fact that they will be separated from SCPs by a glass barrier; consequently, they feel comfortable observing them through the glass.
Medical staff have been visiting morgues since the very beginning of their training, so the sight of dead bodies does not frighten them.
Security personnel, meanwhile, are specifically trained to handle potential encounters with SCP objects. As a result, they maintain a firmer grip on their weapons and remain "on high alert" when engaging targets.
## How does this manifest in the game?
Every level of fear — with the exception of "none" — imposes negative effects on your character. Your mood drops, aiming becomes more difficult, you begin to tremble, and your vision grows blurred.
These are all basic negative modifiers, and their intensity depends on your current fear level.
You can cope with them in several ways, but the most obvious is to simply avoid the source of the fear. Fear is your brain's signal that *this* is something to be avoided for the sake of your own safety. Listen to your instincts.
However, if you find yourself forced to face it, [bold]try having a drink.[/bold] Alcohol dulls the effects of fear.
You can also [bold]close your eyes.[/bold] If you can't see *it*, then there's nothing to be afraid of. Right?
## So, Where Are the SCP Objects?
Beyond the fact that various SCP objects are, naturally, frightening in different ways, some of them can actually weaponize your fear for their own ends.
SCP-106’s sadistic tendencies are common knowledge by now, so it will come as no surprise to you that he [bold]hunts for fear[/bold]. Therefore, whatever you do, do not let him catch you — for if you do, you will be dragged into his [bold]horrific pocket dimension[/bold], where all your previous troubles will seem like **nothing** at all.
## Character Traits
Along with the Fear system, new character traits have been added that introduce various minor mechanics related to fear. Give them a try — it might be fun.
